Definition: properly, a log (as round); by implication, an idol
BiblicalUsage: I take gillûwl to mean idols, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 45 times, and Leviticus and Deuteronomy show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: gillûwl matters to me because an idol is whatever I trust instead of God, and God will not share His glory. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
